ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kokoro wa, nanika o shiru no?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. It's like a big game of "connect the dots," but with lots of math and computers, you see? (Sūpā sutōrī to kompyūtā no tode)

But here's the thing: just because the creators don't fully understand how it works, it doesn't mean it's not working well. These networks are really good at doing certain tasks, like recognizing pictures or generating text. (Eigo ga, nanika o hanasu no?)

It's like a magic trick, but instead of a magician, it's a bunch of math and computers doing the magic. And just like a magician, the creators can make it do cool things, but they don't always know how it's doing it, you know? (Majisuku, nanika o shiru no?)

So, even though the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, they're still really powerful tools that can do some amazing things. (Taisetsu na mono, nanika o shiru no?)
